Brief: Tell me about the Hubble Space Telescope and what it has discovered. — about Initial instruments

1. When launched, the HST carried five scientific instruments: the Wide Field and Planetary Camera (WF/PC), Goddard High Resolution Spectrograph (GHRS), High Speed Photometer (HSP), Faint Object Camera (FOC) and the Faint Object Spectrograph (FOS).
2. WF/PC used a radial instrument bay, and the other four instruments were each installed in an axial instrument bay.
3. WF/PC was a high-resolution imaging device primarily intended for optical observations.
4. It was built by NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, and incorporated a set of 48 filters isolating spectral lines of particular astrophysical interest.
5. The instrument contained eight charge-coupled device (CCD) chips divided between two cameras, each using four CCDs.
6. Each CCD has a resolution of 0.64 megapixels.
7. The wide field camera (WFC) covered a large angular field at the expense of resolution, while the planetary camera (PC) took images at a longer effective focal length than the WF chips, giving it a greater magnification.
8. The Goddard High Resolution Spectrograph (GHRS) was a spectrograph designed to operate in the ultraviolet.
9. It was built by the Goddard Space Flight Center and could achieve a spectral resolution of 90,000.
10. Also optimized for ultraviolet observations were the FOC and FOS, which were capable of the highest spatial resolution of any instruments on Hubble.
11. Rather than CCDs, these three instruments used photon-counting digicons as their detectors.
12. The FOC was constructed by ESA, while the University of California, San Diego, and Martin Marietta Corporation built the FOS.
